Scope: src/core/enrollment.ts:113-116 adds a runtime guard for a missing `ids` argument by casting the parameter to `{ guildId?: GuildId

id?: MemberId } | undefined`. The task's M1 and Context make the *type* the guard ("`ids` is a required sixth parameter with no default, so a five-argument call is a type error"), and the exam pins exactly that with the never-called `// @ts-expect-error` site at tests/enrollment.test.ts:355-358, proven by `bunx tsc --noEmit` (exit 0 in CHECK EVIDENCE). The guard is unreachable for any typed caller and the cast locally weakens the declared parameter type. Harmless as written

INTERFACES gate: `initialState(members)` is declared in Consumes but is never imported or called anywhere in the diff. `readSchedulingState` (src/app/jobs.ts) open-codes the identical initial shape instead (`proposedStartUtc: null`, `proposedBy: null`, `countersUsed: {}`, `confirmedBy: []`, `lockedStartUtc: null` for a freshly-created pairing). Behaviourally equivalent today, but it duplicates a constructor the core module owns, so a future field added to `SchedulingState` would be set in `src/core/scheduling.ts` and silently missed here. Spread `initialState` and override the rebuilt fields.

Copy-pasted logic across the two exam files: the ~65-line `Recorder implements DiscordPort` class (plus `type CallName`, `type Call`, `of()`, `postsIn()`, `buttonIds()`) is duplicated verbatim in tests/app.test.ts and tests/e2e-month.test.ts. It also duplicates what the task's own Produces contract already supplies: `FakeDiscord` records every call in a public `calls` array and exposes `postsTo`, and the implementer additionally wrote `callsOf`, `postsIn`, `threadFor` and `reset` on it - of which only `postsTo` is ever called (one assertion, tests/app.test.ts leg (b))

`callsOf`, `postsIn`, `threadFor` and `reset` are dead. Both files then cast the fake with `as unknown as ...`, discarding the typed `FakeCall` union in a repo that gates on `tsc --noEmit`. The Recorder's stated justification ('the task does not pin the shape of the fake's own calls entries') does not hold - the Context pins it, and the implementer authored it. Either move `Recorder` into tests/helpers/fake-discord.ts (a declared FILES path) so it is written once, or drop it and assert against `FakeDiscord.callsOf('createVoiceChannel')` / `postsTo()` directly with no cast.

The shipping default copy is never rendered by any test. Both exams run on an inline TOML whose `[guilds.copy]` overrides every placeholder-bearing template (`proposal`, `counter`, `one-confirmed`, `locked`, `room-open`, `tz-changed-locked-call`, `met-everyone`, `admin-pair-infeasible`) with `{start}`-shaped strings, while `DEFAULT_COPY` in src/config/copy.ts uses `{time}` for the scheduling templates. `renderCopy` throws on a placeholder with no value, so the `{start}` -> `{time}` alias in `copyVars` (src/app/jobs.ts) is load-bearing for any guild that does not override its copy - which is the Task 15 live install. I traced every `say`/`renderCopy` call site and the defaults do all resolve, so this is a coverage gap rather than a live crash, but nothing in the diff would catch a regression in that alias. Add one case to tests/app.test.ts that drives a pairing to `locked` on a config with no `[guilds.copy]` table and asserts the introduction, proposal, one-confirmed and locked posts render without throwing.

`handleAdminStatus` (src/app/handlers.ts) builds its three lines inline with `ephemeral([...].join('\n'))` and never calls `renderCopy(cfg, 'admin-status', ...)`, so the `admin-status` CopyKey and its DEFAULT_COPY entry ('Pool: {pool}. Holding: {holds}. Upcoming calls: {upcoming}. Reconnections: {reconnect} of recent pairings.') are dead configuration: an admin who sets `copy.admin-status` in their TOML gets nothing. This is not the implementer's error - M8 demands three literal lines (`pool: `, `open pairings: `, `reconnection share:

%`) that the Task-9-owned default template cannot produce, and the submission discloses the choice in a comment at tests/app.test.ts. Reconciling it means changing the `admin-status` default in src/config/copy.ts to a line-shaped template with `{pool}`/`{open}`/`{share}` placeholders, which is outside this task's FILES.

Proof leg (f) / M6 as written is unsatisfiable: it asks for 'a pairing completed with no thread messages, no buttons and no partner Yes'. The only route to `completed` from `locked` is `follow-up-due`, and `locked` is only reachable via two `confirm` events, which makes `tapped` true for both members, so `isSilent({posted:false, tapped:true, partnerYes:false})` is false and neither row can get `needsAck`. The submission discloses this in a comment and reads it through the Context's 'a pairing ends at completed or expired', driving a negotiation timeout to `released` then `expired` and asserting `expect(['completed','expired']).toContain(ended.state)`. That divergence is disclosed and correct, so it is lawful - recorded here so the leg text can be fixed rather than re-argued. Note also that the natural `completed`-with-silence path does exist (a `released` pairing with thread activity takes `release-review` -> `enterCompleted`, which emits `say('follow-up')`, leaving the member who never posted silent)
leg (f)'s third case fires `yes:<pairingId>` at an already-`expired` pairing instead, a state in which the app never offers that button.

The Context's rebuild rule and the pure state machine disagree about counters after a timezone repropose. `readSchedulingState` derives `countersUsed` by counting proposals per `proposedBy` (exactly as the Context prescribes), but `repropose` in src/core/scheduling.ts resets `countersUsed: {}` when a locked call is re-proposed under a new timezone. Because state is rebuilt from rows on every event, that reset is discarded on the very next event: a member who spent their counter before the timezone change still reads as spent, so `handleCounter` refuses them the fresh counter the machine just granted. Nothing in M1-M10 or the Proof legs covers the tz-repropose-then-counter sequence, so the exam is green either way. Fixing it means either dropping the reset from `repropose` (src/core/scheduling.ts, outside FILES) or giving the rebuild a way to ignore proposals older than the newest repropose (src/app/jobs.ts, inside FILES) - the Context text has to pick one first.

concern: plan-defect: src/core/scheduling.ts emits say('proposal', {start}) and say('one-confirmed', {by}) while DEFAULT_COPY for proposal/counter/one-confirmed/locked/tz-changed-locked-call spells the placeholder {time}, and renderCopy throws on an unfilled placeholder. Rather than edit either module I pass `start` and `time` as the same epoch-ms instant, so whichever spelling a server's copy uses renders. A peer test that calls renderCopy itself with only one of the two names against a template using the other will throw inside its own call, which I cannot prevent from here.

concern: plan-defect (observation, no code change): the partnerYes limb of isSilent is unreachable at the moment a pairing completes, because outcomes are only recorded after the follow-up post. M6's 'a partner's yes clears needsAck for both' is therefore implemented in the follow-up button handler via recordEvidence on both members, and a 'notyet' clears it for neither.

The port converts three structural failures into apparent successes carrying an empty id, instead of an explicit error path. src/adapters/discord/client.ts:387 returns `{ id: sent?.id ?? '' }`, so a channel resolved by channelOf that has no `send` (a category, a voice room) reports a successful post and hands the app '' as a message id

:376 does the same for a created thread with no id, and :428 for a created voice channel. The app then stores '' as a channel or message id and a later post/delete against it fails far from the cause. Every other failure in this file throws with a message naming the guild or channel (:342, :352, :371, :426) -- these three should too. postedAt (src/adapters/discord/client.ts:218) has the same shape: a message with neither createdTimestamp nor createdAt records activity at epoch 0 rather than saying it could not read the time. None of this is reachable from the exam's fakes, and real discord.js objects carry all four members, so it blocks nothing.

A throw while handling an interaction is logged and then dropped (src/adapters/discord/client.ts:509), leaving the interaction unanswered: the member sees Discord's "application did not respond" rather than anything the bot said. The same handler will also throw a second time, into the same catch, if app.handle succeeds but interaction.reply fails because the token has already been used. The task does not require a failure reply, so this is advisory, but a followUp-or-reply fallback in the catch would turn a silent dead end into a sentence the member can read.
